description: Ex-Royal Australian Navy Auster coded NW-865, flying on the Australian civil register as VH-NVY. Part of the HARS airworthy flying fleet.
Ex-US Army Cobra on static display at Albion Park. A second HARS Cobra, 76-22592, is at the Parkes annexe.
Ex-Royal Australian Navy Iroquois registered VH-NVV.
Ex-RAAF Iroquois registered VH-X9S to HARS after repair. ADF-Serials notes it operating from the Air Affairs facility at Nowra, so its day-to-day base may not be Albion Park.
Forward fuselage only. Ex-Qantas VH-EAG, later RAAF A20-627; the tail fin and rudder went to the Qantas Founders Museum at Longreach in 2010.

Ex-Qantas short-body 707 donated to HARS by John Travolta in 2017 as N707JT. Dismantled in the United States during 2025 and shipped to Australia; reassembly at Shellharbour Airport was under way during 2026 and it will remain a static exhibit.
The Qantas 747-400 that set the London to Sydney non-stop record in 1989; flown into Illawarra Regional Airport on 8 March 2015 for permanent static display.
Boeing Stearman biplane trainer in the HARS collection.
Long-term restoration project incorporating components of A19-148.
Light twin flown as part of the HARS fleet.
Light twin in the HARS collection.
Centre-line twin in the HARS collection.
Australian ultralight homebuilt. The survey list supplying the HARS inventory shows a dash against this entry and an unassigned registration VH-KFL one line away, so no registration is recorded.

HARS Wirraway. Sources conflict on identity: one survey column pairs it with A20-99, which is elsewhere reported at the Warbirds Aviation Museum Mildura, while a photo caption on the same page calls it CA-16 A20-458. Serial deliberately left blank.
Ex-RAAF Winjeel used by 76 Squadron as a forward air control aircraft; flown as VH-KHZ then re-registered VH-EAD in 2005. Airworthy in silver scheme. Part of the HARS airworthy flying fleet.
The first production CAC Sabre. Displayed at the Mildura Warbirds Museum, donated to the Bankstown museum in 1999 and moved to the HARS hangar at Albion Park in November 2006. Static display.
CAC Ceres agricultural aircraft developed from the Wirraway. No registration is recorded for this airframe in the survey list used.
Rebuilt by HARS using the rear fuselage of A7-087 and wings from A7-012 and A7-022, painted in the Roulettes Fanta Can scheme and mounted on a pole outside HARS on 11 April 2016.
Ex-Royal Australian Navy Catalina registered VH-PBZ and displayed as A24-362/OX-V. Part of the HARS airworthy flying fleet.
Convair 340/440-series airframe; part of the HARS flying fleet as the Convair 440.
Australian single-seat homebuilt designed by John Corby.
Ex-RAAF Mirage withdrawn in October 1987 to RSTT Wagga, later at Air World Wangaratta and Essendon; now on static display at HARS.
aliases: Mirage IIIO; Mirage; Dassault Mirage III

description: Ex-RAAF Tiger Moth registered VH-DHV. Part of the HARS airworthy flying fleet.
Owned by the late Fr Jeremy Flynn, HARS chaplain, and registered VH-FJW for Father Jeremy Wish. Under restoration to airworthiness at Albion Park.
Formerly displayed at the Australian Aviation Museum Bankstown; now in ground-running condition at HARS Albion Park.
Australian-built Vampire fighter modified for RAAF public relations and recruiting displays.
Ex-Royal Australian Navy Sea Venom displayed as 870/NW. Static display.
Australian-built three-engined feederliner of the type used by the Royal Flying Doctor Service; part of the HARS flying fleet.
Fuselage only.
Acquired by HARS from Oakey in 2011 with A4-234 and six semi-trailer loads of spares as the Vietnam Veterans Memorial Flight; registered VH-VBA. Part of the HARS airworthy flying fleet.
Departed Oakey for Albion Park on 2 November 2011 with A4-210; registered VH-VBB.
Ex-Royal Australian Navy Dakota coded 802/NW, registered VH-NVZ.
Ex-RAAF Dakota auctioned in June 2000 and now VH-EAE, displayed as A65-95/PK-L. Part of the HARS airworthy flying fleet.
Ex-RAAF Dakota, latterly with Base Flight Richmond as VMJMN; now VH-EAF.
Four-engined Douglas transport in the HARS collection.
Static display at HARS Albion Park.
DC-3(C) in the HARS flying fleet.
Acquired by HARS and initially displayed at the Australian Aviation Museum Bankstown; relocated to Albion Park in March 2010 and externally restored.

Full-scale flying replica of Charles Kingsford Smith Southern Cross. Airworthy. Recorded without a registration: the genuine VH-USU Southern Cross is preserved at the Sir Charles Kingsford Smith Memorial at Brisbane Airport and this airframe wears its marks.
aliases: Southern Cross; FVIIa; Fokker FVII; VH-USU

description: Fokker Friendship in the HARS collection.
Fokker Friendship in the HARS collection.
Australian-developed target drone; airframe number 31.
Ex-RAAF F-111C on static display at HARS Albion Park.

Ex-Royal Australian Navy Tracker coded 845. The assets of the RAN Historic Flight including this aircraft were acquired by HARS and held in secure outside storage courtesy of Air Affairs Australia pending transport to Albion Park.
Ex-Royal Australian Navy Tracker coded 851.
Ex-Royal Australian Navy Tracker coded 844, registered VH-NVX; the airframe HARS intends to return to flight.
Ex-Royal Australian Navy Sea Fury transferred from the Fleet Air Arm Museum to HARS, where it has been refurbished; displayed as 110/NW.
Czechoslovak light twin in the HARS collection.
The HARS Lockheed Super Constellation recovered from the United States in 1996 and maintained in running condition; the museum centrepiece and the focus of regular engine-run days.
Ex-RAAF Orion registered VH-ORI and maintained by HARS in flying condition.
aliases: AP3; AP3C; P-3; P3; Orion; VH-ORI

description: Ex-French Navy P2V-7 Neptune coded 566, registered VH-LRR.
Ex-RAAF Neptune registered VH-NEP.
Ex-RAAF Neptune with 5476 flying hours, registered VH-IOY in 1981 and kept airworthy by HARS; described by the museum as the only flying Neptune in the world.
Polish-built SB Lim-2A two-seat trainer version of the MiG-15 carrying Polish air force number 607.
aliases: MiG15; MiG15UTI; SB Lim-2; Lim-2; Lim2

description: Polish-built Lim-6bis registered VH-ALG and carrying Polish air force number 434.
Two-seat MiG-21 trainer registered VH-XXI.
Italian twin-engined utility aircraft on static display.
Twin Pioneer short-field transport, part of the HARS flying fleet.
Pressurised turboprop twin retaining a United States registration.
Australian-designed light aircraft.
Victa R.2 prototype.

Ex-Royal Australian Navy Wessex embarked in HMAS Success in 1986, later a training aid at RSTT Wagga Wagga; returned to the Fleet Air Arm Museum by road on 7 December 2015 and now with the HARS collection at Albion Park.
Ex-Australian Army Kiowa, on loan to the Museum of Army Aviation at Oakey and in service with the Army Helicopter School; sold to HARS Albion Park in August 2017.
Czechoslovak agricultural aircraft, listed by one survey as a JZD-37.
